text.p: These are the major headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister challenged on jobs, Quebec: Chretien often put on defensive in peppery interchanges at taping of TV show.
- Topless stroller wins appeal: No harm done, panel judges say.
- Top UN hopefuls hit rough sailing: Four candidates get potential veto.
- Hong Kong tycoon picked to take over: Tung favoured by Chinese for chief.
- New Brunswick loosens fiscal belt with tax cuts: Plan will raise consumer confidence, Premier Frank McKenna says.
- Royal to open merchant bank: Committing $500 million and a pair of high-profile hires to buy big stakes in small firms.
- Jumbo bails out of video rentals: U.S. firm pays $9.5 million for Canada's No. 4 chain as big players continue to take over industry.
- General Motors cut-rate financing: Canadian unit attempts to reverse decline in market share.
- Canadian Pacific Rail wants unions to reopen contracts: Eastern division at risk, president says.
- Canadian Pacific Railway may sell east network: Says it must have concessions fro unions and lower municipal taxes if it is to keep 6,246 kilometres of track in Eastern Canada and the U.S.
- Are banks finding their own share prices a bit too steep?
